What to look for in winter gloves

  • Knuckle and palm protection. Look for hard or moulded knuckle armour and palm sliders that resist abrasion.
  • Waterproofing. A membrane like Gore-Tex or Drystar keeps hands dry — vital for safe control in UK rain.
  • Fit and feel. Gloves should be snug with no loose fingertips so you keep full control of the levers.
  • Season-specific. Vented summer gloves and insulated winter gloves do very different jobs — many tourers own both.

Frequently asked questions

How much should I spend on winter gloves?

Our catalogue spans £40.49 to £379.99. Budget options under £150 cover the essentials, the £150–£400 mid-range hits the sweet spot for most UK tourers, and premium picks above £400 add refinement, lighter materials and longer-term durability.

Which brands are worth considering?

Popular, well-reviewed brands in this category include Macna, Five, Merlin, Tucano, Spada. All are stocked by SportsBikeShop with UK warranty support.

Do I really need waterproof kit?

In the UK, yes. Cold, wet hands and feet impair control and concentration within minutes. A waterproof membrane is one of the best touring upgrades you can make.

faq.q: Are heated gloves worth it over insulated gloves?
faq.a: If you ride below about 5C regularly, yes. Insulation only slows heat loss, so on long cold rides fingers still chill. Heated gloves such as the Macna Rafino or Merlin Bednell add active warmth, keeping hands working when standard winter gloves cannot.

faq.q: How long do heated glove batteries last?
faq.a: Battery run time depends on the heat level, typically two to six hours per charge. On the lowest setting most kits last a full commute, but a cold all-day tour may need a mid-ride recharge or a hardwired bike feed. Always carry the charger.

faq.q: Do winter gloves keep you dry as well as warm?
faq.a: The best ones do. Look for a Gore-Tex or Raintex membrane alongside the insulation, as on the Five HG Prime and Macna Rafino. Warmth without waterproofing fails fast in UK rain, since wet insulation chills your hands rapidly.

faq.q: Should winter gloves fit tighter or looser?
faq.a: Slightly roomier than summer gloves, so a trapped air layer can insulate, but not so loose that fingertips bunch. If they are too tight they restrict circulation and actually make hands colder. Try them with any liner glove you plan to wear.
